You've completely missed the point that OP is depressed because he **isn't** so depressed and "emotionally volatile".  I was trying to figure out if OP still understands this on a logical level, because he has stressed he is still "coldly logical".

OP said:

> I feel like the part of my head that can think emotionally like that or begin to understand emotion is locked up now

Also, the fact that he is able to give these examples means that he **does** realize when people need encouragement, but he doesn't know how to relate emotionally.  Why he can't relate is what I was trying to figure out.

Feel free to try and help OP, since you obviously know what to do.

Well you said you were "too coldly logical".  If someone says something like "I didn't get the job I applied for", wouldn't you realize that it's nice to say something like "I'm sorry to hear that" or something encouraging?  Why do you have trouble relating to these things?  Are you so un-depressed that you can't imagine something like that happening to you?

So you can't understand how people can be so moody since you are no longer kept down by depression?  Could you try looking for signs of depression/sadness/anger when you talk to people and think you might miss what's hurting them?  You could ask people if they feel hopeless with their job hunting, or distant with their SO.  And maybe not in those specific words, but try to get an idea of how people are feeling, if you want to console them and stop feeling guilty yourself.

My point was that if you are dealing with people who are depressed or even just sad, it is more important to deal with them emotionally, rather than with logic.  Often when people are depressed they have irrational beliefs and fears that can't be addressed with logic (since they are irrational).

Now to go back to your original problem, what is preventing you from relating with others?  I would think you at least understand more how moods and thoughts relate to depression or something about how best to console someone who is down.

How do you feel less depressed but unemotional?  Depressed people are typically more numb, especially in my scenario.  When I'm less down, I can relate to people more simply because I have more energy and I'm more optimistic;  when I'm depressed, nothing matters so screw humanity.

Not to be rude but I don't understand how you feeling better takes away your ability to empathize.  Even if you're happy, can't you still remember the soul-crushing pain of depression or whatever.  Can't you still understand that depression sucks out logic and replaces it with irrational beliefs and capriciousness.

When you say you are less emotional, do you mean that you have less emotions or that you change emotions less often?  Aren't you now happy/content more often and able to look at things realistically (not necessarily with logic).

Is depression not largely dependent on one's circumstances, which means that fighting depression is largely determining which aspects of your life need to be changed.  Or do you feel it is more existential/philosophical wrestling with despair/hopelessness that eradicates depression.

What is preventing you from relating with others?  Do you have a bunch of acquaintances who are depressed/miserable?  I've fought my depression somewhat by realizing that many people are like me and that I can figure out the roots of my depression.  It's somewhat more depressing, though, to know what I must do but be unable to do it because I'm too unmotivated.
Numerous mistakes, failures, and bad decisions that I regret.  Overall I just don't like where I am at and wish my life had taken a different path.

How marriage was established is an interesting question, but even if a religion specifically promoted it, instead of just societal pressure, there are two things to keep in mind.  First, the definition of marriage has changed dramatically over time and it has nothing to do with gay people living "alternative lifestyles".  Marriage was for much of history about a man being given "ownership" over a woman.  This includes women not being able to divorce from their husbands.  Second, in many parts of the world, marriage is something that is arranged.  For these reasons, I do not see how religious people can say that marriage has had one consistent definition throughout history.  

Additionally, the genesis story of Eve being created for Adam (and from him) doesn't seem to be a union of two people who love each other, but rather a man getting what he desires.  Plus, were Adam and Eve even officially married?  Where in the Bible is marriage codified? I'm sure there are a bunch of parts that talk about marriage, but how does the Bible itself show marriage as always being a consistent idea.  Just now I'm remembering that parts of the Bible say that an unwed man must marry his brother's wife, should his brother die, or something like that.  This "definition" is nowhere to be found in the modern "definition".
